answers.evidence:
**All 10 test cases pass** (output from `go test -v`):

| Test | Description | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `TestReverseList_Empty` | nil head → nil | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseList_SingleElement` | [42] → [42] | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseList_TwoElements` | [1,2] → [2,1] | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseList_MultipleElements` | [1,2,3,4,5] → [5,4,3,2,1] | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseList_NegativeNumbers` | [-3,-2,-1,0,1] → [1,0,-1,-2,-3] | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseList_DuplicateValues` | [7,7,7,7] → [7,7,7,7] | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseList_LargeInput` | 1000-element list reversed correctly | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseListRecursive_Empty` | nil head → nil | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseListRecursive_SingleElement` | [99] → [99] | ✅ PASS |
| `TestReverseListRecursive_MultipleElements` | [10,20,30,40] → [40,30,20,10] | ✅ PASS |

**Edge cases covered:**
- Empty list (`nil`)
- Single element (identity reversal)
- Two elements (simplest non-trivial case)
- Multiple elements (standard case)
- Negative and zero values
- Duplicate values (same value throughout)
- Large input (1000 elements) — verifies no stack overflow on iterative version

**Benchmarks:**
```
BenchmarkReverseList-16            66,541 ops   19,264 ns/op   16,000 B/op   1,000 allocs/op
BenchmarkReverseListRecursive-16   64,216 ops   19,301 ns/op   16,000 B/op   1,000 allocs/op
```
